text:
maria_sales: FYI Acme reached out — POC decision needed. They want EU data residency, recommendations on hosted vs dedicated vs private, answers for the security questionnaire, and a 4-week timeline. Success metrics they care about: latency p95, throughput (300 rps), functional accuracy on our eval prompts, and cost guidance. Can we align on a recommended path by EOD tomorrow?

sam_eng: my quick take — start hosted in the eu region for fastest ramp, run their eval prompts against a suggested model variant, then switch traffic to a dedicated pool for steady-state if throughput/latency needs exceed the hosted SLOs. private on-prem should be a later phase (compliance/legal takes time).

olivia_ps: agree with @sam_eng. We should also define concrete success criteria so legal and procurement can sign off:
- Eval pass rate >= 90% on the provided prompt set
- Latency p95 < 250ms for typical requests
- Error rate < 0.5% during load tests
- Cost target: keep incremental serving cost under $200 per 1M tokens for the workload profile
Proposed 4-week sprint: W1 infra + region setup, W2 prompt tuning & baseline evals, W3 load & latency tuning (dedicated if needed), W4 security review + handoff.

lee_sre: some infra notes: hosted (EU) is quickest but we need to confirm model size & seq len distribution. Dedicated requires reserved GPU pool — estimate 2–4 weeks to provision for nvlink clusters depending on availability. Private requires customer infra + our on-prem package + KMS integration. Also note: KV-cache warmup and batching config will materially affect p95.

sam_eng: for the eval run we can smoke-test quickly. curl example to hit hosted EU endpoint (replace API_KEY):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer API_KEY' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-medium-eu","input":"<prompt here>","max_tokens":256}'
```
Use that to validate model/output before we spin up dedicated.

maria_sales: quick pricing Q — what's the floor for dedicated monthly commitment and typical lead time? Customer wants budget numbers for procurement.

olivia_ps: ballpark (non-binding): small dedicated pool starts ~€9k–€12k/month (reserved), mid-size ~€25k+/month. Private (on-prem license + support) typically starts in the mid-5-figures annual and depends on node count + support tier. Lead time: hosted = hours, dedicated = 2–6 weeks, private = 6–12+ weeks (legal + infra).

sec_bot: Security questionnaire stub: https://redwood.internal/sec-q/ACME-POC — contains DPA, data residency, KMS/HSM options, audit log requirements. Please fill the submittable before W2 so we can approve private/dedicated plans.

maria_sales: perfect — I'll forward this summary to the customer and ask them to share the prompt set + sample payloads. Will schedule a 30m sync tomorrow 10:30 to finalize. :thumbsup:

sam_eng: will prepare a short runbook for the hosted baseline and a checklist for dedicated provisioning (GPU types, expected seq len, batch settings).

lee_sre: I'll prepare an ops note on monitoring (token-level cost, per-route latency, KV cache hit metrics) to include in the POC dashboard.

olivia_ps: I'll draft the success-criteria doc and the procurement ballpark numbers to send to Acme.

maria_sales: thanks all — deadline EOD tomorrow to lock approach.
